_readme: Curated September 2026 calendar. Sale fields: date (YYYY-MM-DD, sorts the list), dateLabel, sale, house, city, url, note, flag, flagUrgent. Optional 'lots' array: artist, title, year, estimate, url, note. Facts taken from published catalogues; every note is our own. Never copy catalogue descriptions.

sales.note: Decorative arts, silver, textiles and rare books. A large share is over a hundred years old, which makes it non-exportable from India whoever buys it.

lots.title: Himalaya, numbered edition
lots.note: Roerich is one of the nine artists declared an art treasure in 1979. Whether a numbered print edition falls inside that scope is not obvious, and the answer decides whether you can take it home.

lots.title: Four first editions and view books
lots.note: Books and records of historical interest reach the antiquity threshold at seventy-five years rather than a hundred. All four are well past it.

sales.sale: The Auction: Inside The Devil Wears Prada 2
sales.note: Online costume and jewellery sale, thirty-five lots. Low estimates and heavy bidding. Nothing here touches export restriction, but check materials on the exotic-skin handbag lots before shipping anywhere.

sales.sale: Hiroshige: Colors of the Four Seasons, The Alan Medaugh Collection
sales.note: 181 Hiroshige woodblock prints, lots 1 to 181. Japanese prints move freely, but note Christie's own banner on EU cultural goods licensing if the work is heading to Europe.

sales.sale: South Asian Modern and Contemporary Art
sales.note: 112 lots, the strongest South Asian sale of the month. Works already outside India are not caught by the 1972 Act, so this is the corridor to use if you want a modern Indian work you can actually ship.

lots.title: Building in Trafalgar Square
lots.note: Top lot of the sale. Sitting in New York, so exportable in a way the same artist would not be from a Mumbai saleroom.

lots.title: A Progression of Sails
lots.note: Thin secondary market at this level. Check how often works of this scale have actually sold before setting a number.

sales.note: Six lots only, Warhol, Banksy and Picasso. Sterling settlement, so an Indian resident should budget the remittance before the estimate.

sales.sale: Ritual, Cosmos, and Imperial Splendor: Important Chinese Art
sales.note: 62 lots of early Chinese bronzes, Buddhist sculpture and imperial ceramics. Archaeological material carries provenance and import-licensing questions in several jurisdictions. Read the conditions before you bid, not after.
Modern Indian painting, 75 lots. Domestic sale, so no remittance and no import duty for Indian residents. For overseas buyers, check each lot's export status individually.

lots.title: Christ in a Village
lots.note: The largest number in any Indian sale this month. At this level the buyer's premium and tax alone will run to a substantial sum, so settle those before the room opens.

lots.title: Untitled
lots.note: Bawa's market has been strong and thin at once. Worth checking unsold rates rather than only achieved prices.

sales.note: Around 200 lots including a long run of early bronzes. Saffronart marks many of these NON-EXPORTABLE REGISTERED ANTIQUITY in its own catalogue. If you are bidding from outside India, read that line on every lot.

lots.title: Vishnu flanked by Ayudhapurushas, early 9th century bronze
lots.note: Marked non-exportable registered antiquity. You may own it; you may not take it out of India. Price the restriction in.

lots.title: Standing Sridevi, 16th century bronze
lots.note: Also non-exportable, despite having previously sold at Christie's New York in 2007. Once an antiquity is in India and registered, it stays.

sales.note: 81 lots. Two of the nine art treasure artists appear here, which makes this the clearest export test of the month for any overseas buyer.

lots.title: Untitled, pencil and watercolour
lots.note: Sher-Gil was declared an art treasure in December 1976. This cannot leave India. A Gulf or diaspora buyer would own a work they could never bring home.

lots.title: Untitled, mountainscape
lots.note: Declared an art treasure in August 1979. Same restriction, at a fifth of the price. If you want a Navratna work and intend to keep it in India, this is the accessible entry point.

sales.sale: Modern and Contemporary South Asian Art
sales.note: Sale L26500. Includes works by Rabindranath Tagore, one of the nine, but held outside India and therefore not caught by the 1972 Act. This is the distinction most buyers get wrong.

lots.title: Mithuna Crimson
lots.note: Previously in the Chester and Davida Herwitz collection and shown at the Worcester Art Museum in 1974. Exhibited provenance of that quality is rare and worth paying for.

lots.title: Works on paper
lots.note: A Tagore in London is exportable; the same artist in a Mumbai saleroom is not. The 1972 Act does not reach works already abroad before the notification.
